_about: Known deviations of the models from reference data, shown to users in the interface. Each entry names the components (any order), the model, the kind of deviation, a message and its reference. Entries of kind 'ternary-azeotrope' make the matching ternary azeotrope test run as 'todo', so the test run reports when the entry can be removed. Remove an entry as soon as a fix resolves it.

issues.message: The ternary azeotrope comes out at 69.95 °C and 7.7 / 9.3 / 83.0 wt % (ethanol / water / ethyl acetate), close to the handbook value of 70.3 °C and 7.8 / 9.0 / 83.2 wt %. The model predicts that this liquid splits into two liquid phases (tangent-plane test), so the real boiling point is a vapour in equilibrium with two liquids; the flash calculates it (P-VF flash, VF = 0): 69.99 °C for the handbook liquid, which the model splits into two liquids. The shaded two-liquid region shows only the spinodal, which is narrower than the real split.
issues.reference: Azeotrope tables, Wikipedia (from Lange's Handbook, 10th ed., and CRC Handbook, 44th ed.)

issues.message: Water and ethyl acetate boil as two liquid phases at 70.4 °C (heterogeneous azeotrope). This diagram assumes one liquid and shows a minimum of 70.1 °C at water mole fraction 0.37, inside the real two-liquid region; the shaded band shows only the spinodal. The flash calculates the two liquids and the three-phase point: 70.61 °C, vapour water mole fraction 0.313.
issues.reference: Azeotrope tables, Wikipedia (from Lange's Handbook, 10th ed., and CRC Handbook, 44th ed.)

issues.message: The UNIQUAC set for ethanol + cyclohexane (ChemSep databank) predicts two liquid phases at 323-338 K (at 338 K between ethanol mole fractions 0.30 and 0.55), so at 1 atm it boils as two liquids. The open excess-enthalpy data of Lien et al. (2003) were measured as one liquid over the whole composition range at 323.15 K, and the 1-atm azeotrope (64.9 °C, 69.5 wt % cyclohexane) is tabulated without liquid layers. Use NRTL for this pair. No open binary vapour-liquid data was found to refit UNIQUAC; a refit to the azeotrope alone also splits.
issues.reference: Lien, Lin, Lee, J. Chem. Eng. Data 48 (2003) 359, excess enthalpy at 323.15 K (data public in the NIST TRC ThermoML Archive); azeotrope from Wikipedia 'Azeotrope tables' (Ponton, Azeotrope Databank, 2001)
